source_context: The Padovan sequence (OEIS A000931): P 0 = P 1 = P 2 = 1, P (n+3) = P (n+1) + P n. This is a three-term linear recurrence, unlike the two-term Fibonacci/Lucas-style sequences already in the corpus (fibonacci-q-matrix, lucas-numbers, horadam-cassini-identity, sylvester-sequence-coprimality), so it is not an instance of the existing LeanFrontier.Horadam.W framework and is not a trivial specialization of an already-accepted general result. The module proves positivity (every term is at least 1) and a telescoping partial-sum identity, (sum_{i<n+1} P i) + 2 = P (n+2) + P (n+3), derived by rewriting each term as P n = P (n+3) - P (n+1) and telescoping; the additive '+2' form is used instead of a subtracted '-2' form so that no truncated natural subtraction appears in the statement. Absence evidence, searched over the pinned Mathlib tree including Archive and Counterexamples: case-insensitive 'padovan' and 'perrin' return no hits at all outside this submission; 'motzkin' hits only Mathlib/Tactic/Linarith (the Fourier-Motzkin elimination oracle) and Counterexamples/Motzkin.lean, an unrelated topological counterexample; 'zeckendorf' and 'beatty' do occur (Mathlib/Data/Nat/Fib/Zeckendorf.lean and Mathlib/NumberTheory/Rayleigh.lean), which is why neither was chosen instead. Mathematics is classical and not claimed as new; the subject choice, Lean statements, and proofs were produced by the model without human mathematical direction beyond the general task of finding an uncovered area. padovan_add_three, the additive restatement of the defining recursive equation, is public (so downstream users can rewrite with it without unfolding padovan) but is not claimed as an entrypoint, matching the sylvesterNumber_succ precedent in sylvester-sequence-coprimality.json: it is exactly the definitional equation and is closed by rfl, so listing it as an entrypoint would invite a trivial-baseline rejection rather than adding a genuine claim.
